_comment: DragonBreak Online skill template. Consumed by the extended mastery system (see SKILLS_DESIGN.md). Tiers are 1-5; thresholds are hours of server-verified activity in that skill. Every <...> is a form id to fill once the marker spells exist in DragonBreak Online Edits.esp.
_pointSystemComment: The use-based point system from server/SKILLS_DESIGN.md. While enabled is false the server runs the three-chosen-skills ladder above and nothing here is read. Turning it on converts each character's record the first time it is read: hours become levels at 30 units an hour, so everyone lands in the tier they already hold. pool is the total levels one character may hold across all skills, capPerSkill the ceiling for one, seatAbove/seatCount the Seat rule (how many skills may pass 90), expertAbove/expertCount the same for 75, transferFloor the level no skill falls below when another takes from it, bucketBurst/bucketPerHour the token bucket that caps work per hour, dailyCaps the per-skill ceiling per day by band, characterDaily the whole character's.

skills.label: Blunt
skills.title: The Heavy Hand
skills.description: Maces, war axes, warhammers and battleaxes, one hand or two: the weapons that break armour and bone by weight, as Oblivion counted them. Tiers raise your proficiency.

skills.label: Archery
skills.title: The Far Shot
skills.description: Bows and crossbows. Tiers raise proficiency.

skills.label: Blade
skills.title: The Keen Edge
skills.description: Swords, daggers and greatswords, one hand or two. A blade is a blade: the skill that cuts and thrusts, as it was before Skyrim split the hands. Tiers raise your proficiency.

skills.label: Defense
skills.title: The Wall
skills.description: Blocking with shields and weapons, and wearing armor well. One skill drives vanilla Block, Light Armor and Heavy Armor.
tiers: Medium armor, blocks cost less stamina, worn armor +25%
Heavy armor, shield bash, worn armor +75%
Worn armor +150%, power bash, arrows deflected
Worn armor +250%, blocks reflect part of the blow, no stagger from small hits

skills.label: Arcane Arts
skills.title: The Ordered Mind
skills.description: Destruction, Conjuration and Illusion. The only way to learn spells from tomes, studied at any spell study point (the Synod Conclave in Bruma to start). Three spells known at a time; the tier decides the highest spell rank you may learn.

skills.label: Martial Arts
skills.title: The Closed Fist
skills.description: Fists and staves. Every blow of your fists drains your opponent's stamina, and a tired fighter hits weakly, so a boxer who stays on someone wears them down; armour stops fists more than it stops a weapon, and a landed unarmed power attack knocks the weapon from their hands. Quarterstaves and battle staves strike fast and partly through armour. Only this skill grows their damage, never Blunt. A Khajiit's claws count as fists.

skills.label: Blacksmith
skills.title: The Forge-Bound
skills.description: Only a Blacksmith may use the forge, the workbench and the grindstone. Tiers decide which metals you may work and how well you improve gear.

gates.hint: a forge, an anvil or a smelter

tiers: Steel, silver, dwarven, elven, chainmail, mithril

skills.label: Alchemist
skills.title: The Patient Hand
skills.description: Only an Alchemist may use the alchemy lab. Tiers decide the strength of the potions and poisons you can brew.

counts._comment: Brewing is the work (alchemy.js awards each brew); gathering plants and trees is the Harvesting trade's, and eating an ingredient teaches nothing, as in vanilla (Nate, 2026-09-30: Alchemist rose from picking mushrooms). The lab itself still counts until the brew award is live.

skills.label: Woodcutter
skills.title: The Grain Reader
skills.description: Only a Woodcutter may use chopping blocks, the charcoal kiln and the lumber mill. Tiers lengthen the chopping mini-game and raise mill yield.
tiers: 20 strikes, fine charcoal, best mill yield

skills.label: Miner
skills.title: The Deep Delver
skills.description: Only a Miner may work ore veins. Tiers decide which ores you can mine and how much a vein gives.

counts._comment: PickaxeMining is deliberately NOT here: Bruma has 169 PickaxeMining* FURN markers and a bare activation on one would credit the skill with no minigame and no ore. It stays in gates.stations so the markers remain miner-only.

skills.label: Tailor
skills.title: The Fine Thread
skills.description: Only a Tailor may use the tailor's bench. All clothing and medium armor is made here; tiers decide what you can cut and sew.

skills.label: Skinner
skills.title: The Far Tracker
skills.description: Only a Skinner may skin animals and use the tanning rack. Tiers decide the strips, leather and quantity you get.
tiers: 3 leather per pelt, rare pelts intact

skills.label: Scholar
skills.title: The Ink-Stained
skills.description: Only a Scholar may read the books of the world. Books are nodes, not loot: reading is a mini-game with a chance at copies, and a small chance at a spell tome or scroll.
tiers: Read common books; now and then a scroll, rarely a novice spell tome
Better copies; now and then a novice spell tome
More and stronger scrolls; apprentice spell tomes

skills.label: Enchanter
skills.title: The Rune-Wright
skills.description: Only an Enchanter may use the arcane enchanter, on weapons, armour and jewellery. You learn an enchantment by disenchanting an item that carries it; tiers decide how strong your enchantments can be.
tiers: Up to half the strength of the finest enchantments found
Up to three quarters of their strength
Up to half again their strength

skills.label: Priest
skills.title: The Hand of the Divines
skills.description: Restoration and Alteration. The only way to learn healing and warding spells, studied at any spell study point. Praying at a shrine counts as Priest work and raises the odds of a blessing.

skills.label: Cook
skills.title: The Hearthkeeper
skills.description: Only a Cook may use cooking pots and ovens. Tiers decide the quality of food you can prepare.

craftWeight._comment: What one dish is worth in units of work (GroundedPasta and swag, 2026-09-30: cooking rose too slowly and a complex dish was worth no more than a simple one). Read by masterySystem (skillPoints.craftWeightOf): byTier[t-1] when the recipe carries the Cook tier gate DBO_Skill_cook_T<t> (tools/recipes), otherwise byIngredients[n] for n ingredients, the last entry for more. Never below the product-value weight every craft had before (0.5 for any dish). The same dish again within the hour still counts less (1/(1+k/8)) and the hourly bucket (pointSystem.bucketPerHour, 30) still caps the hour. Needs a restart.

skills.label: Harvesting
skills.title: The Gleaner
skills.description: Gathering from the world's resource nodes: plants, mushrooms, nests, and gold pouches. Without this skill a node gives little or nothing; tiers raise both the chance of a yield and the amount.

harvestablePlacedItems._comment: placed ingredient refs treated as nodes (Harvesting roll, then empty until respawn) instead of blocked clutter; matched by base EditorID prefix

kinds: FLOR (all flora: flowers, mushrooms, nests, planted crops such as cabbage, potato, leek, wheat, gourd, carrot, tomato, farm rows)
TREE harvestables (apple, snowberry, juniper, jazbay and any tree or bush with a harvest ingredient)
hanging food and herb bundles (see harvestablePlacedItems)
Hearthfire garden and planter soil (BYOH planters)

skills.label: Lockpicking
skills.title: The Quiet Hand
skills.description: Opening what others locked. Only two things can be picked: player-owned doors and dungeon loot chests. Tiers decide the lock level you can attempt. The same quiet hand picks pockets: sneak up on someone and press X, and the better you are, the better your odds.

vanillaLevel.levelFrom: sum of tiers across the three chosen skills divided by 3, rounded down
vanillaLevel.perLevel: +10 to one of Health, Magicka, Stamina chosen by the player

minigames.mining: timing bar, one strike per hit inside the green zone, strikes per vein by Miner tier
minigames.woodcutting: rhythm press, strikes per sitting by Woodcutter tier (4-20)
minigames.reading: word-order or timed page turn, result rolls the Scholar tables
minigames.lumberMill: no mini-game, 30-minute cooldown per player per mill, yield by Woodcutter tier

spellStudyPoints.name: The well in the Hall of the Elements
spellStudyPoints._comment: Until the Study Magic activators (DragonBreak Online Edits.esp, DLE v8) are in the load order; they replace this point then (Nate, 2026-09-30). add more entries later: temples, mage towers, a court wizard's study

spellStudyPoints.name: The Synod Conclave in Bruma
spellStudyPoints._comment: Whole cells, no refr: anywhere in the Conclave (CYRBrumaSynodConclave) or its basement (CYRBrumaSynodBasement), until the Study Magic activators (DragonBreak Online Edits.esp, DLE v8) are in the load order; then only within radiusMeters of one (Nate, 2026-09-30: "make StudyMagic activators the study points"). Read by server\spells.js, which also accepts cell + refr + radiusMeters, and places + requires (tools/spells/study_points.py writes those).

praying._comment: Anyone can pray, but only at a shrine of the deity chosen after character creation. Other shrines answer with a notice and no roll. Priests get better odds and skill progress. server\prayer.js reads deities.choices[].shrines. (The Divines' shrine index that used to sit here, read by nothing, went on 2026-09-28: Nate.)
praying.minigame: hold the prayer key through three verses; releasing early ends the prayer with no roll

deities._comment: Picked after character creation, or by praying at a shrine while godless (server\prayer.js offers it). Stored per character in private.dboDeity. Praying works only at your own deity's shrines, or at an aspect of them (see auriel.aspectOf). Conversion: /deity <name> at that deity's shrine, conversionCooldownDays apart, current blessing removed. The menu key the brief asks for is front work and is not built; /deity is the stopgap.

choices.name: Akatosh
choices.sphere: Time. Chief of the Divines, the Dragon God whose covenant with Alessia binds the Empire.

choices.name: Arkay
choices.sphere: The cycle of birth and death, and the sanctity of the grave. His priests bury the dead so they stay buried.

choices.name: Dibella
choices.sphere: Beauty, love and art. Her temple at Markarth keeps the Sybil; her Cyrodiilic chapels teach that beauty is a form of worship.
choices.replacedBoon: Persuasion +10, vanilla (dead: no NPCs to persuade).

choices.name: Julianos
choices.sphere: Wisdom, logic, literature and law. Patron of mages and of the Elder Council that writes the Empire down.

choices.name: Kynareth
choices.sphere: Air, wind, sky and the elements. The only Divine who was present at the making and stayed.
alsoKnownAs: Kyne (Nordic), the Kiss at the End

choices.name: Mara
choices.sphere: Love, compassion and the hearth. The Mother-Goddess, worshipped in every province under one name or another.

choices.name: Stendarr
choices.sphere: Mercy, charity and justice; the shield against the unnatural. His Vigilants hunt Daedra and the undead.

choices.name: Talos
choices.note: Openly worshipping Talos is a crime in Cyrodiil in 4E 201. prayer.js warns a Talos worshipper the first time they pray, and nothing else happens: whether the guards care is a faction decision for Nat, not a prayer one. private.dboLawful already exists if it should.
choices.sphere: Tiber Septim, the man who became the Ninth Divine and founded the Empire that outlawed him.
choices.unlawfulWhere: The Empire, under the White-Gold Concordat. Bruma is Imperial and the Thalmor keep a Justiciar presence.
choices.replacedBoon: Shouts return 20% sooner - dead, or at least unconfirmed: nobody has established that shouts work on this server at all, and a boon nobody can verify is not a boon.

choices.name: Zenithar
choices.sphere: Work, commerce and honest labour. The god who says wealth follows craft, and never the other way round.
choices.replacedBoon: Speechcraft +10, vanilla (dead: no merchants, no barter).

choices.name: Auri-El
choices.note: The Aldmeri name for Akatosh, not a separate god. prayer.js treats the two as one: a worshipper of either may pray at either shrine. Vanilla places Auri-El's shrine only in the Forgotten Vale; Nat placed one in Bruma county on 2026-09-21 (DragonBreak Online Edits.esp:12AE03, BSHeartland, near 57257,205947), the only one reachable under the region lock.
choices.sphere: The Aldmeri aspect of Akatosh, worshipped by the Snow Elves as the founder of their line.
choices.boon: Marksman raised by 10, for half a day.

choices.name: Malacath
choices.note: Custom shrine activator placed at six strongholds and Gol-Kharzum.
choices.sphere: The sworn oath, the broken curse, and every people the others cast out. Trinimac was, and Malacath is.
choices.boon: Damage raised by 10% and Block by 15.

choices.name: Azura
choices.sphere: Dusk and dawn, prophecy, and the Moonshadow. The kindest of the Princes, which is not saying much.

choices.name: Boethiah
choices.note: Vanilla Skyrim shrine is a static; only the Solstheim one activates.
choices.sphere: Plots, secret murder, treason - and the teacher who makes the Chimer strong by testing them to destruction.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Her sacrament is the murder of one's own follower. Imperial law draws no line between a rite and a killing, whatever the Tribunal once taught.

choices.name: Mephala
choices.sphere: Lies, sex and secret murder; the Webspinner, who taught the Morag Tong their trade.
choices.note: Not one of Oblivion's fifteen: she is kept because her Solstheim shrine is real and Beyond Skyrim has modelled CYRShrineMephalaTEMP in an Ayleid ruin. Her vanilla boon duplicates Zenithar's; Illusion or Pickpocket would suit the Webspinner better, but it is Bethesda's record and is left alone. Not one of Oblivion's fifteen: she is kept because her Solstheim shrine is real and Beyond Skyrim has modelled CYRShrineMephalaTEMP in an Ayleid ruin. Her vanilla boon duplicates Zenithar's; Illusion or Pickpocket would suit the Webspinner better, but it is Bethesda's record and is left alone.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Secrets, and the assassin's contract. The Morag Tong holds a licence in Morrowind and is outlawed everywhere else; in Cyrodiil her worship is read as conspiracy before it is read as faith.

choices.name: Mehrunes Dagon
choices.sphere: Destruction, change, revolution and ambition. Bruma above all others has met him: the Great Gate opened here, and Martin broke it.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Bruma above every other place in Tamriel. The Great Gate of 3E 433 opened outside these walls and the city was all but lost; the cathedral at its heart is dedicated to St Martin, who died ending that invasion. To kneel to Dagon here is not heresy, it is the war returning.
choices.replacedBoon: Damage +10%, which duplicated half of Malacath's.

choices.name: Molag Bal
choices.sphere: Domination and the enslavement of mortals. The King of Rape; the father of vampires; the reason a black soul gem is black.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Domination, and vampirism with it. The Imperial courts read his cult as enslavement and murder in one, and a confessed worshipper is hunted rather than tried.
choices.replacedBoon: An absorb-health effect that would have had to be authored from scratch.

choices.name: Nocturnal
choices.sphere: Night and darkness, luck, and things that are not where they were left. The Nightingales answer to her; nobody else gets an answer.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Patron of thieves, and of the Nightingales sworn to her. The kneeling is not itself the crime - the oath taken at her altar is.

choices.name: Hircine
choices.note: DBO_ShrineOfHircine activators on the Daedric Shrines AIO statues: Falkreath forest (BearCaveMill cell) and Solstheim (Snowclad Ruins). Named by its DBO_ShrineOf* base ACTI, which exists only on the statues the 2026-09-14 activator pass placed.
choices.sphere: The Hunt, the Chase and the Great Game. The Huntsman of the Princes; werewolves are his.
choices.boon: Stamina returns three times as fast - the hunt never tires.
choices.replacedBoon: Stamina returns 10% faster (the text until 2026-10-01). The record, DBO_BlessingOfHircine, has always been FortifyStaminaRateFFSelf 10: StaminaRate +10 on the base 5, which the game and now the server's regeneration tick (prayer.js) count as three times the stamina regeneration.
choices.unlawfulWhere: The Hunt, and the lycanthropy that comes with it. The Vigil of Stendarr hunts his followers, and a werewolf in an Imperial county is put down rather than charged.

choices.name: Meridia
choices.note: Named by REFERENCE, not by base, on purpose: the base DA09MeridiaStatue also stands four times in CYRCrowhavenBurialHalls as scenery and those must not become shrines. Two references are named - the vanilla Kilkreath activator (4e4d6, in Skyrim) and the one placed at the Namira test site on 2026-09-20 (125bf8).
choices.sphere: The energies of living things, and a hatred of the undead so total that she is counted a Daedric Prince mostly by process of elimination.
choices.replacedBoon: The undead flee you, on TurnUndeadFFMassSelfArea - wrong, and only found by dumping the template: a shrine blessing is a fire-and-forget SELF spell, so a mass-self-area turn undead fires once at the shrine and never again.

choices.name: Sanguine
choices.note: DBO_ShrineOfSanguine activators: the Rift (33,-18) and inside Misty Grove. Named by its DBO_ShrineOf* base ACTI, which exists only on the statues the 2026-09-14 activator pass placed.
choices.sphere: Revelry, debauchery and passionate indulgence. The only Prince most people would drink with twice.
choices.boon: Hunger comes on half as fast - the feast does not end.
choices.blessingRecipe: Copy AltarDibellaSpell exactly; FortifyPersuasionFFSelf (fb98a:Skyrim.esm) at 10, duration 28800. It duplicates Dibella's boon, which is left deliberate: she charms and he carouses, and vanilla already gives Zenithar and Mephala the same Speechcraft.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Drink and revelry, which the Empire's own feast days already brush up against. Forbidden on paper and ignored in practice.
choices.blessingDesign: Persuasion was the wrong answer twice over: it does nothing here, and it was the least Sanguine thing on the list. The Prince of indulgence belongs on the one system this server has that is actually about appetite - private.needs. While blessed, hunger accrues at half rate. prayer.js exposes __dboPrayerHungerMult and the gamemode's needs tick multiplies by it; no plugin work, no spell, nothing for the Creation Kit to do.

choices.name: Sheogorath
choices.note: DBO_ShrineOfSheogorath activator in the Hjaalmarch marsh (-12,24) near Morthal. Named by its DBO_ShrineOf* base ACTI, which exists only on the statues the 2026-09-14 activator pass placed.
choices.sphere: Madness. Was Jyggalag, and will be again, and is not, and both of those are true.
choices.boon: Whatever he feels like. A different god's blessing every time, chosen at random.
choices.blessingDesign: The one boon that is more lore-accurate as code than as a record: prayer.js rolls one of the OTHER deities' blessings and grants that instead. The Madgod needs no spell of his own, and a worshipper who prays twice gets two different gods. Implemented in prayer.js as `capricious: true`.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Madness. Cyrodiil treats the Mad God as superstition rather than sedition - a shrine to him draws warding signs from the neighbours, not the Legion.

choices.name: Clavicus Vile
choices.sphere: Power through bargains. Every wish is granted exactly as worded, and the wording is never yours.
choices.boon: The bargain: you name the boon you want and Vile takes a price for it.
choices.blessingDesign: A boon of another god, granted in full, against a standing cost - reduced maximum health for as long as it lasts. prayer.js can do this with no new record: it already grants and revokes spells. Needs a choice step in the widget, which is why it is not built yet.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Bargains. Proscribed like the rest, but the courts care what was traded away - a name, a soul, a life - far more than they care about the prayer.
choices.note: DA03ClavicusVileShrine, the vanilla Haemar's Shame shrine, which is a TACT (a talking activator) rather than an ACTI - it is activated the same way. Placed at the Bruma test site on 2026-09-20; the base is named, so the Skyrim one counts too.

choices.name: Hermaeus Mora
choices.sphere: Knowledge, memory and the fate of all things. He does not bargain; he collects.
choices.boon: What you read teaches you more, and books find you.
choices.blessingDesign: Server-side, like Sanguine's (scholarBoon): while blessed, a finished reading round counts twice for the Scholar skill (gamemode.js reading), and a dungeon chest or body can hold a skill book besides its loot (dungeons.js scholarBookChance). Nate, 2026-09-28: 'give a scholar xp and drop buff', drops for books.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Forbidden knowledge. Half of any College's restricted shelf is his under another name, so a scholar caught at it is disciplined far more often than charged.

choices.name: Namira
choices.sphere: The ancient darkness, decay, and everything that revolts: spirits, spiders, the eaten dead.
choices.boon: Sneak raised by 10, and you see in the dark.
choices.note: The Ring of Namira feeds you on corpses, which this server could do properly - it already has corpse looting and skinning. That version belongs with the needs system, not with a spell. The Ring of Namira feeds you on corpses, which this server could do properly - it already has corpse looting and skinning. That version belongs with the needs system, not with a spell.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Cannibalism. Her rite requires eating the dead - a capital crime in every Imperial province, and an offence against Arkay on top of it.

choices.name: Peryite
choices.sphere: Pestilence, and the ordering of the lowest realms. The weakest of the Princes, and the one most concerned with tidiness.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Pestilence. His cultists are few and already sick; the Empire quarantines them more often than it prosecutes them.
choices.replacedBoon: A resist-disease effect that does not exist, with Fortify Block as a stand-in.

choices.name: Vaermina
choices.sphere: Dreams and nightmares, and the memories torn out of them.
choices.unlawfulWhere: Nightmares harvested out of sleeping people, who cannot refuse her. The courts treat that as torture and nothing softer.

choices.name: The Hist
choices.sphere: The great trees of Black Marsh, older than memory, whose sap made the Saxhleel what they are. The Hist remembers, and it gives.
choices.boon: Health regenerates 50% faster while the blessing lasts - the sap remembers.
choices.replacedBoon: Histskin (PowerArgonianHistskin e40d5:Skyrim.esm), once a day: a racial power, which the client dispels the moment it is used (magicSyncService BLOCKED_POWER_IDS: "Racial powers are disabled on this server"), so until 2026-10-01 this blessing gave nothing that worked.
choices.blessingDesign: Histskin's own theme, made passive: the server's regeneration tick (prayer.js) adds half the race's health regeneration again while the blessing runs. Between Meridia's +25% and the Worm Cult's +100%, as the faiths' rarer, shorter blessings run a little stronger than the Princes'.

choices.name: The Ancestors
choices.sphere: The honoured dead of House and family, the heart of Dunmer faith. The Tribunal is gone since the Third Era; the New Temple keeps the ancestors and the three Good Daedra.
choices.boon: Fire spells burn you a quarter less while the blessing lasts - the dead of your House stand in the flame with you.
choices.replacedBoon: Ancestor's Wrath (PowerDarkElfFlameCloak e40d4:Skyrim.esm), once a day: a racial power, which the client dispels the moment it is used (magicSyncService BLOCKED_POWER_IDS: "Racial powers are disabled on this server"), so until 2026-10-01 this blessing gave nothing that worked.
choices.blessingDesign: Fire damage taken x0.75 while the blessing runs: gamemode.js blessingCombat target.ancestors, element fire (a hit whose effects are resisted by Resist Fire, the MGEF resist value, as the game resists a fire spell, a dragon's breath or a flame cloak). The Dunmer's fire, turned to a ward; Trinimac turns 25% of all spells.

choices.name: The Yokudan Gods
choices.sphere: The gods the Redguards brought from drowned Yokuda: Satakal the world-skin, Tu'whacca who guards the Far Shores, and HoonDing, the Make-Way god who clears the path when the people need one.
choices.boon: Stamina returns twice as fast while the blessing lasts - HoonDing makes the way.
choices.replacedBoon: Adrenaline Rush (PowerRedguardStaminaRegen e40ce:Skyrim.esm), once a day: a racial power, which the client dispels the moment it is used (magicSyncService BLOCKED_POWER_IDS: "Racial powers are disabled on this server"), so until 2026-10-01 this blessing gave nothing that worked.
choices.blessingDesign: Adrenaline Rush's own theme, made passive: the server's regeneration tick (prayer.js) doubles the race's stamina regeneration while the blessing runs, as the Worm Cult's doubles magicka.

choices.name: The Riddle'Thar
choices.sphere: The Two-Moons Dance, the Khajiiti faith of Masser and Secunda and the Riddle-Thar, the cosmic order that shapes every Khajiit by the moons of their birth.
choices.boon: You see in the dark while the blessing lasts, as the moons' children do.
choices.replacedBoon: Night Eye (PowerKhajiitNightEye aa01d:Skyrim.esm), whenever you wish: a racial power, which the client dispels the moment it is used (magicSyncService BLOCKED_POWER_IDS: "Racial powers are disabled on this server"), so until 2026-10-01 this blessing gave nothing that worked.
choices.blessingDesign: The Khajiit's Night Eye for the blessing's length: cast on the worshipper (dboCastSelf) from DBO_BlessingOfVaermina, the one plain Night Eye spell in the server's load order (NightEyeEffect and the shrines' Cure Disease, 8 h). The client's Active Effects page names it the Blessing of Vaermina; a record of Riddle'Thar's own is a plugin follow-up.

choices.name: Trinimac
choices.sphere: The Aldmeri warrior god and champion of Auri-El, strongest of the elven gods before Boethiah devoured him and he rose again as Malacath. Some Orsimer still keep his name, and most of their kin despise them for it.
choices.boon: Armor raised by 50 and 25% of magic resisted while the blessing lasts.

choices.name: The Dragon Cult
choices.unlawfulWhere: The Dragon Cult was broken in the Dragon War and its priests entombed; to keep its rites is an old Nordic heresy, rarely pressed in Cyrodiil but never forgotten.
choices.sphere: Worship of the dragons as the children of Akatosh and rightful lords of mortals, served by masked Dragon Priests who ruled in their name in ancient Skyrim.

choices.name: The Worm Cult
choices.unlawfulWhere: Necromancy is hunted in the Empire since the Mages Guild's war on the King of Worms, and a Worm Cultist found out can expect the Legion or worse.
choices.sphere: The followers of Mannimarco, the King of Worms, who seek mastery over death itself. Not vampires and not common cultists, but necromancers bound to a god of their own making.

deities._placements: Measured, not assumed: server\shrine-placements.json, regenerate with py ck-mcp\shrines.py. placements = every reference of this deity's shrine bases in the load order; inPlaytest = those inside the region lock; inBruma = those in Bruma county, the only released and walkable part of Beyond Skyrim Cyrodiil. A deity with inBruma 0 cannot be prayed to until Skyrim opens.
deities._lore: The roster is the canonical one for Cyrodiil, not whoever happened to have a shrine already: the Nine Divines plus Auri-El, and Oblivion's fifteen Daedric shrines plus Mephala. JYGGALAG IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT - he was Sheogorath until the Greymarch ended in 3E 433 and has walked free since, but he has no cult, no shrine and no worshippers in 4E 201, and a shrine to him would be the one thing in this list that lore actually forbids. Every boon below is grounded in the Prince's sphere, and every magic effect it names exists in this load order (measured by ck-mcp\blessings.py; see server\blessing-effects.json).
deities._blessingSource: vanilla = a real SPEL that works today, whether Bethesda's or one of the eleven DBO_BlessingOf* records authored on 2026-09-20 by SSEEdit 4.1.5f\Edit Scripts\DBO_Blessings.pas. server = the gameplay does it and no record exists (prayer.js; for the Ancestors, gamemode.js blessingCombat). pending = a boon still waiting on a spell; there are none left.
deities._deadStats: NO BOON MAY BE A DEAD STAT. This server is entirely player-run: no merchants, no dialogue, no barter, and no speech skill among the eighteen. Persuasion, Speechcraft and Pickpocket therefore do nothing at all, and four boons that used them have been replaced (see replacedBoon). Where the replacement overrides a vanilla shrine, Bethesda's record is left untouched on disk and skills.json simply points elsewhere, so reverting is one line. Check any new boon against what this server actually runs: combat and the damage formula, health/magicka/stamina and their regen, carry weight, sneak, the magic schools, alchemy, lockpicking, and the needs meter - all real; anything that needs an NPC to talk to - not.
deities._authored: The eleven DBO_BlessingOf* SPELs live at DragonBreak Online Edits.esp:1209BF-1209C9. Each is a copy of AltarNocturnalSpell - a fire-and-forget SELF spell, NOT a constant ability - with one effect swapped and CureDiseaseEffect kept, 28800 s. Namira is the exception: she keeps Fortify Sneak and her second effect is Night Eye instead of cure disease, which suits the Prince of decay. Re-running the script is safe; it leaves records that already exist alone.
deities._testSite: Nat placed a statue of every Prince at the Namira shrine site (CYRNamirasShrineExterior and around it, grid 23,47) on 2026-09-20 as one central place to test worship. They went in as STATICS, which the engine never fires an activation on; DBO_ShrineActivators2.pas gave each Prince a DBO_ShrineOf* ACTI using that same statue mesh and repointed the references at it, so the statue itself is the shrine.
deities._lawComment: lawful/unlawfulWhere are Imperial law as it stands in Bruma, not Dunmer temple doctrine - the Tribunal's "good Daedra" (Azura, Boethiah, Mephala) are not the three the Empire tolerates. Malacath, Azura and Meridia are openly legal; the rest are proscribed, and unlawfulWhere carries how hard that is enforced, from "hunted" (Mehrunes Dagon, Molag Bal, Namira, Boethiah, Vaermina) down to "ignored in practice" (Sanguine, Sheogorath, Hermaeus Mora, Clavicus Vile, Peryite). Talos is unlawful under the Concordat. prayer.js reads only the boolean; the prose is what a player is told.

respec._comment: Standing stones are the only place to change your three chosen skills. Activating a stone opens the K menu in respec mode.
respec.where: standing stones (vanilla DoomStone activators: Warrior, Mage, Thief, Lover, Steed, Lady, Lord, Apprentice, Atronach, Ritual, Serpent, Shadow, Tower)
respec.whatHappens: drop any of the three skills and pick replacements; dropped skills lose all tier progress; no swap cooldown applies at a stone (the gold is the cost)

worldPickup._comment: Nothing lying in the world can be picked up with E. Loose items placed by the plugins are not loot. Resources come from nodes (Harvesting, Mining, Woodcutter), containers, crafting and trade. Items dropped by players (dynamic ff-space refs) stay pickable so trading and dropping keep working.
worldPickup.farmsAndFields: Open to everyone with the Harvesting skill. No ownership lock on crops: protecting a field is roleplay (guards, patrols, bounties), not a mechanic.

edition.decision: Skyrim SE 1.6.1170 with the four free base creations only. No Anniversary Edition requirement.
edition.revisit: Alternative Armors packs (crafting variety) and player homes, launch-day decision only.
